A cookie is a small file placed on your computer or mobile device when you visit a website which helps our site and our 3rd party advertising and data partners recognize your device the next time you visit the site. Cookies are essential for many simple functions such as recognizing a repeat visitor as logged in, and providing access to your account, favorites, playlists, and profile. Audiomack utilizes two common types of cookies - session based cookies (which expire once you close your web browser) and persistent cookies (which stay active until deleted or deactivate after a set period of time). Other technologies include pixel tags (transparent images which help us determine if a page or email has been viewed by a user), web beacons (also known as web bugs, which serve a similar function to pixel tags), and web storage. Additionally, mobile users may be tracked using Device ID and/or hashed data to identify repeat mobile usage. These combined technologies are used both by Audiomack and our 3rd party partners to ensure essential Platform functionality; target, serve, measure, and track advertising delivery, targeting, optimization, and performance; measure Platform analytics and usage; and to measure user and audience behavior, trends, demographics, and location.

The Platform contains links to third-party content, advertisements, and sites that are not owned by nor affiliated with Audiomack Inc.. We cannot be held accountable for the content or privacy policy of third- party sites. Be sure to read their privacy policies to determine if you are comfortable with how they handle your information.

Wurl Advertising | Scene-level supply at scale - Wurl
Wurl Advertising brings together premium streaming TV inventory, trusted data partners, and real-time content signals to deliver the largest unified source of scene-level CTV supply.
With real-time visibility into what’s on screen and how audiences engage, Wurl helps advertisers capture more attention in scenes that are relevant and brand safe.
Wurl’s interoperable platform underpins scene-level targeting solutions for top contextual targeting providers - so advertisers can transact using the IDs they prefer.

In streaming TV, contextual relevance and brand safety change scene by scene. Wurl’s scene-level targeting helps ads appear alongside content that feels timely—driving stronger attention, recall, and performance.
Built from Wurl’s proprietary data on viewing behavior across the streaming TV ecosystem, our audience segments help advertisers find and reach high-value viewers—wherever they’re watching.
How is AI used to analyze the content on a scene-by-scene basis?

Wurl’s proprietary system uses a large language model (LLM) to evaluate and classify the dialog, sounds, and imagery of content as it is passed for distribution. The content is automatically assigned tags across emotion, genre, and brand safety. As Wurl identifies the content being streamed, these tags are appended to the content metadata before it is sent to DSPs, where the segments can then be targeted.
How is Wurl Advertising’s scene-level targeting different from other contextual targeting solutions available in the market?
We use GenAI to determine what is happening on the screen, at scene level. This means that you can achieve greater contextual precision than traditional contextual targeting solutions in CTV.
Using an open integration model, Wurl enables contextual data partners to scale their bespoke models across our inventory access and scene-level insights.

Wurl Advertising’s flexible marketplace lets advertisers transact using the Deal IDs and targeting methods that best align with their goals. Advertisers can activate contextual targeting from leading data partners—including KERV.ai, IRIS.TV, Peer39, and Wurl’s proprietary solution, Moment Match—all across Wurl’s scaled CTV inventory.
– Aligns ad to content based on the emotional tone of the scene directly before the ad break (ex: Joy, Anger, Surprise).
– Targets specific types of content present in a scene (ex: Sports, Travel, Comedy). For example, advertisers can target sports scenes, even if the overall program is not sports-focused.

In-stream ad formats capture attention by keeping viewers engaged with the content they’re already watching. Because playback continues, viewers are less likely to disengage—driving higher attention, stronger recall, and more memorable brand experiences. These ads are often placed during natural lulls in the content, such as live sports timeouts, rolling credits, or scene transitions, making them feel additive rather than disruptive.

With Wurl Advertising, in-stream ads can be targeted using the same scene-level contextual targeting and brand-safety controls as traditional linear ad breaks, ensuring brand messaging appear alongside appropriate content.
